governanceNotes: D1 batch 29 (2026-09-23): deferred. The management literature (Brockman 2022 aspiration-sclerotherapy series and the urology reviews) characterizes epididymal cysts and spermatoceles as benign incidental findings with no documented downstream morbidity, so no catalog target (chronic-pelvic-pain-syndrome, complex-regional-pain-syndrome, unexplained-chronic-pain, testicular-atrophy, varicocele-hydrocele, testicular-torsion) has association evidence; a post-surgical chronic-pain edge would attribute to the cyst identity what the literature attributes to the surgical procedure itself (wrong-identity guard, batch-25 contractures precedent).

Reproductive-effect attribution (obstruction of epididymal ducts) is discussed in review literature as a theoretical concern but lacks outcome quantification, and the catalog holds no male-infertility identity to receive the edge; reopening condition: cohort evidence of cyst-attributable outcomes (pain syndromes, obstructive azoospermia with a catalog identity) would justify re-screening.
